pairs.evidence: clients/typescript/src/sync.ts:329 The incremental drain stops on a short page despite an available continuation, so a server-clamped page can end the run before the backlog is drained.

techniques.evidence: clients/typescript/src/types.ts:80 The SDK uses the feed's timestamp/rowid sort tuple rather than an offset; the standard permits tuple tokens for non-key ordering, and the inspected server constructs them from the last returned row.

clients/typescript/src/client.ts:56 The paginated method's documentation describes positioning but does not state cross-page consistency or concurrent-write effects; searches of the SDK README, source, and linked SDK documentation found no such contract.

clients/typescript/src/client.ts:1 This context consumes dataset reads without merging authorization policies or exposing recursive listing; searching the package found no implementation of those constructs.

clients/typescript/src/sync.ts:146 The configurable 500-revision default has no documented memory target, worst-case item size, overhead factor, or derivation; the low-level client's 1000-item default is likewise underived.

clients/typescript/src/sync.ts:326 Although the loop checks continuation absence here, line 329 also terminates on a short page; requesting batchSize above the server's 1000 ceiling therefore stops after one clamped page even when next_cursor is present.
